title: Credit creation in a one-bank economy
body: Assume an economy with only one commercial bank and no currency held by the public. Mr Arun deposits Rs 1,000 in the bank, which to begin with keeps the whole amount as reserves with the Reserve Bank of India. The RBI fixes the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) at 10 per cent. The bank lends as much as the CRR allows. Every loan is spent and the money comes back to the same bank as a new deposit, after which the bank lends again. The process continues round after round until the entire Rs 1,000 of reserves is needed as required reserves against the bank's total deposits, and no further lending is possible.
